Solve the **bracket** and **multiplication** simultaneously for speed.

Product: 72 × 2 = 144

Bracket: 61 − 28 = 33

Combine: 144 − 19 + 33 + 35 = 125 + 68 = 193

**∴ The correct answer is 193.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 72 × 2 − 19 + (61 − 28) + 35

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS Rule**

⇒ 72 × 2 − 19 + (33) + 35 (Solving **Bracket**)

⇒ 144 − 19 + 33 + 35 (Solving **Multiplication**)

⇒ 125 + 33 + 35 (Solving first **Subtraction**)

⇒ 158 + 35 (Solving first **Addition**)

⇒ 193

**∴ The correct answer is 193.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule Priority

The order of operations is **Brackets (B)**, **Orders (O)**, **Division (D)**, **Multiplication (M)**, **Addition (A)**, and **Subtraction (S)**. Note that DM and AS have equal priority and are solved from left to right.

Types of Brackets

Brackets are solved in the order: **Bar/Vinculum**, **Parentheses ( )**, **Braces { }**, and then **Square Brackets [ ]**.

questions.question: One angle of a parallelogram is 60 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of its adjacent angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **parallelogram**, the sum of any two **adjacent angles** is always **180°** (they are **supplementary**).

Adjacent Angle = 180° − Given Angle

Adjacent Angle = 180° − 60° = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** One angle of the **parallelogram** = 60°

**Formula Used:** Consecutive **interior angles** formed by a **transversal** crossing **parallel lines** are **supplementary**. For a parallelogram ABCD, ∠A + ∠B = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3c67347894296c6e34e18afa5f275f6b4fe0444646caeedf7d1d3ad558a300d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the angles of the **parallelogram** be ∠A, ∠B, ∠C, and ∠D.

⇒ Given ∠A = 60°.

⇒ Since AD || BC and AB || DC, the **adjacent angles** are **supplementary**.

⇒ ∠A + ∠B = 180°

⇒ 60° + ∠B = 180°

⇒ ∠B = 180° − 60°

⇒ ∠B = 120°

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Opposite Angles Property

In any **parallelogram**, the **opposite angles** are always equal in measure. If one angle is 60°, its opposite angle is also 60°.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all four **interior angles** of a **parallelogram** (or any **quadrilateral**) is always 360°.

Consecutive Angles

Any two **consecutive angles** of a parallelogram are **supplementary**, meaning their sum is 180°.

questions.question: Least Common Multiple of A and B is 15. Least Common Multiple of C and D is 25. What is the Least Common Multiple of A, B, C and D?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of a set of numbers can be found by taking the LCM of the LCMs of its subsets.

LCM(A, B, C, D) = LCM[LCM(A, B), LCM(C, D)]

Given: LCM(A, B) = 15 and LCM(C, D) = 25

Required LCM = LCM(15, 25)

LCM(15, 25) = 75

**∴ The correct answer is 75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of A and B = 15

LCM of C and D = 25

**Formula Used:**

The **Associative Property** of LCM states: LCM(a, b, c, d) = LCM(LCM(a, b), LCM(c, d)).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66763b57da01d336b7c430fb9357c46f4a594c1b6a7bbab6b4cec782b54690e1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ To find the LCM of 15 and 25, we use **Prime Factorization**.

⇒ 15 = 3¹ × 5¹

⇒ 25 = 5 × 5 = 5²

⇒ LCM is the product of the highest power of all prime factors involved.

⇒ LCM(15, 25) = 3¹ × 5²

⇒ LCM = 3 × 25

⇒ LCM = 75

**∴ The correct answer is 75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental LCM Property

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by every number in the given set.

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers x and y, the product of their HCF and LCM is equal to the product of the numbers: **HCF(x, y) × LCM(x, y) = x × y**.

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime** (having no common factors other than 1), their LCM is simply the product of the two numbers.

questions.question: Least Common Multiple of A and B is 30 and C = 18. What is the Least Common Multiple of A, B and C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **LCM** of three numbers **A, B, and C**, we use the property: **LCM(A, B, C) = LCM[LCM(A, B), C]**.

Given **LCM(A, B) = 30** and **C = 18**.

We need to find the **LCM of 30 and 18**.

Check the multiples of the larger number (30): 30 × 1 = 30 (not divisible by 18), 30 × 2 = 60 (not divisible by 18), 30 × 3 = **90** (divisible by 18).

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**LCM** of **A** and **B** = 30

Value of **C** = 18

**Formula Used:**

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of three numbers is the **LCM** of the **LCM** of any two of those numbers and the third number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb68c22fc6677f47fc7c63e5a5675f554670d44c09db3b065f69d2fac1bf7b54.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 30 = 2 × 3 × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3²

⇒ To find the **LCM**, take the highest power of each prime factor present in both numbers:

⇒ Highest power of 2 = 2¹

⇒ Highest power of 3 = 3²

⇒ Highest power of 5 = 5¹

⇒ **LCM(30, 18)** = 2¹ × 3² × 5¹

⇒ **LCM** = 2 × 9 × 5 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF Relation

For any two numbers **a** and **b**, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.

LCM of Fractions

To calculate the **LCM** of fractions, use the formula: **LCM = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators)**.

Divisibility Rule

The **HCF** of a set of numbers always completely divides their **LCM**.

questions.question: The Least Common Multiple of two numbers is 150. Which of the following can be the Highest Common Factor of the two numbers?
questions.solution:

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of any set of numbers must always be a **factor** of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

Given **LCM** = 150.

Check the options to see which number divides 150 exactly: 150 ÷ 15 = 10 (Integer).

Other options (20, 35, 28) do not divide 150 without leaving a remainder.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

questions.question: An article is sold for a loss Rs. 81. Loss percentage is 18 percent. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Loss** of 18% = ₹81

1% = 81 ÷ 18 = 4.5

**Selling Price (SP)** = 100% − 18% = 82%

**Selling Price (SP)** = 82 × 4.5 = ₹369

**∴ The correct answer is ₹369.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Loss** = ₹81

**Loss Percentage** = 18%

**Formula Used:**

**Loss %** = (**Loss** ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** − **Loss**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6843f3adc9423e4a9024eb89a87148dbebe1a0feb95dc3a96e8b96e373339c36.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 18 = (81 ÷ **CP**) × 100

⇒ **CP** = (81 × 100) ÷ 18

⇒ **CP** = 4.5 × 100 = ₹450

⇒ **SP** = 450 − 81

⇒ **SP** = ₹369

**∴ The correct answer is ₹369.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP)

The price at which an article is purchased. It is the base for calculating **Profit %** or **Loss %**.

Profit Percentage Formula

**Profit %** = [(**Selling Price** − **Cost Price**) ÷ **Cost Price**] × 100.

Selling Price for Profit

To find **SP** when **Profit %** is given: **SP** = **CP** × (100 + **Profit %**) ÷ 100.

questions.question: Out of two numbers, 40 percent of the smaller number is equal to 20 percent of the larger number. If the sum of both the numbers is 750, then what is the value of the larger number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Smaller number (S)** to **Larger number (L)** is inversely proportional to their percentage values.

S : L = 20% : 40% = 1 : 2

Sum of ratios = 1 + 2 = 3 units

3 units = 750 ⇒ 1 unit = 250

Larger number = 2 units = 2 × 250 = 500

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of numbers = 750, 40% of Smaller = 20% of Larger.

**Formula Used:** Percentage = (Value / Total) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46814695267fa8ee045f21c5b7e8ddd5482fa4d3d36f74643f9cf32b5b885b97.png] 

Let the **smaller number** be S and the **larger number** be L.

⇒ 40% × S = 20% × L

⇒ (40/100) × S = (20/100) × L

⇒ 2 × S = 1 × L ⇒ L = 2S

⇒ S + L = 750

⇒ S + 2S = 750

⇒ 3S = 750 ⇒ S = 250

⇒ Larger number (L) = 2 × 250 = 500

**∴ The correct answer is 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Equivalence

If x% of A = y% of B, then the ratio of the numbers is A : B = y : x. This is a common shortcut for direct ratio conversion.

Dividing a Sum into Ratios

To divide a total sum T into ratio a : b, the parts are calculated as [a / (a + b)] × T and [b / (a + b)] × T.

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Problems involving the sum of two numbers can always be modeled using x + y = Total and solved by substituting one variable in terms of the other.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the loss of 25 percent. Cost price and selling price are increased by 40 percent and 'y' percent respectively. If the new loss percentage is 15 percent, then what is the value of 'y'?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Let the initial **Cost Price** be 100 units, then the initial **Selling Price** is 75 units (25% loss). New **Cost Price** = 100 + 40% = 140 units. New **Selling Price** at 15% loss = 140 × 0.85 = 119 units. Required percentage increase in **Selling Price** (y) = [(119 − 75) ÷ 75] × 100. y = (44 ÷ 75) × 100 = 176 ÷ 3 = 58.67. **∴ The correct answer is 58.67.**

questions.question: S alone can complete 3/4 part of a work in 18 days. R is 3 times as efficient as S. In how many days will R alone complete the same total work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for **S** to complete **3/4 work** = **18 days**

Time for **S** to complete **full work** = 18 × (4/3) = **24 days**

Since **R** is **3 times** as efficient as **S**, he takes **1/3rd** of the time.

Time taken by **R** = 24 ÷ 3 = **8 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**S** completes **3/4 part** of work in **18 days**.

**R's Efficiency** = 3 × **S's Efficiency**.

**Formula:**

Total Time = (Time taken for fraction) ÷ (Fraction of work)

Efficiency × Time = **Total Work**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **S**
 24
 24
 1
 
 

 **R**
 8
 3
 
 

⇒ Total days for **S** = 18 × (4 ÷ 3) = **24 days**.

⇒ Let **Efficiency of S** = 1 unit/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = Efficiency × Days = 1 × 24 = **24 units**.

⇒ **Efficiency of R** = 3 × **Efficiency of S** = 3 × 1 = **3 units/day**.

⇒ Days taken by **R alone** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of R

⇒ Days taken by **R alone** = 24 ÷ 3 = **8 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the ratio of efficiency is x : y, then the ratio of time taken is y : x.

Total Work Calculation

Total Work = Number of Days × Efficiency. For fractional work, Full Work Time = (Time for Part) × (Reciprocal of the Part).

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their efficiencies are added: Eₜₒₜₐₗ = E₁ + E₂ + ... + Eₙ.

questions.question: M and R together can do a work in 18 days. R and P together can do the same work in 24 days. P and M together can do the same work in 36 days. Working together, how much part of work can they do in 4 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = **LCM**(18, 24, 36) = 72 units.

2(M + R + P) combined efficiency = (72 ÷ 18) + (72 ÷ 24) + (72 ÷ 36) = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9.

Combined efficiency of **M, R, and P** = 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 units/day.

Work done in **4 days** = 4.5 × 4 = 18 units.

Required part of work = 18 ÷ 72 = 1/4.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/4.**

questions.question: Speed of a boat downstream and upstream is 42 km/hr and 36 km/hr respectively. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of boat in **still water** is the average of **downstream** and **upstream** speeds.

Speed = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2

Speed = (42 + 36) ÷ 2 = 78 ÷ 2 = 39 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 39 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Downstream Speed (D)** = 42 km/hr

**Upstream Speed (U)** = 36 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Speed of boat in **still water** (x) = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed of **stream** (y) = (D − U) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62f9f7b1c843637924071be7312a41afd95a3dd178db05cc18d7aa4f5730100e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = (42 + 36) ÷ 2

⇒ x = 78 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 39 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 39 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Stream

The rate at which the water flows is given by y = (Downstream speed − Upstream speed) ÷ 2. In this case, y = (42 − 36) ÷ 2 = 3 km/hr.

Downstream and Upstream Logic

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat (x) + Speed of stream (y). Upstream Speed = Speed of boat (x) − Speed of stream (y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 23 km/hr. If the upstream speed of the boat is 17 km/hr, then what is the speed (in km/hr) of the stream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Speed of Stream** = **Still Water Speed** − **Upstream Speed**

⇒ Speed of Stream = 23 − 17

⇒ Speed of Stream = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the **boat** in **still water** (u) = 23 km/hr

**Upstream speed** of the boat (u − v) = 17 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

**Upstream Speed** = Speed in Still Water − Speed of Stream

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87df136d100eb81dd7ee70cb925585dd8b80156e1103a10fd36bcbd6d2870b10.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the **stream** be **v** km/hr.

⇒ 17 = 23 − v

⇒ v = 23 − 17

⇒ v = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

It is the net speed of the boat when it travels in the direction of the stream: **Downstream Speed = u + v**.

Speed in Still Water

If downstream and upstream speeds are known: **u = (Downstream + Upstream) ÷ 2**.

Speed of Stream

If downstream and upstream speeds are known: **v = (Downstream − Upstream) ÷ 2**.

questions.question: The downstream speed of a boat is 35 km/hr. Speed of stream is 5 km/hr. What will be the total time (in hours) taken by the boat to cover 350 km downstream and 150 km upstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Upstream Speed** = **Downstream Speed** − 2 × **Stream Speed**

**Upstream Speed** = 35 − 2(5) = 25 km/hr

**Total Time** = (350 ÷ 35) + (150 ÷ 25) = 10 + 6 = 16 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Downstream Speed** = 35 km/hr, **Stream Speed** = 5 km/hr, **Downstream Distance** = 350 km, **Upstream Distance** = 150 km.

Formula Used: **Time** = **Distance** ÷ **Speed** | **Boat Speed** (u) = **Downstream** − **Stream** | **Upstream** = u − **Stream**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c444e7bbd0dae121e7e6ebd8feed31c7da4e66ab874ed2bd1e488a94f3428be.png] 

⇒ **Boat Speed in Still Water** (u) = 35 − 5 = 30 km/hr

⇒ **Upstream Speed** (v) = 30 − 5 = 25 km/hr

⇒ **Time taken for Downstream** = 350 ÷ 35 = 10 hr

⇒ **Time taken for Upstream** = 150 ÷ 25 = 6 hr

⇒ **Total Time** = 10 + 6 = 16 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 16 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Boat Speed and Stream Speed Calculation

Boat speed in still water (u) = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2. Stream speed (v) = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed in Boats and Streams

When the boat covers the same distance downstream and upstream, the Average Speed = (u² − v²) ÷ u, where u is boat speed and v is stream speed.

Upstream and Downstream Logic

Downstream speed is always greater than upstream speed because the stream supports the boat movement in the former and opposes it in the latter.

questions.question: The cost price of an article is Rs. 10000. It is sold at a profit of 40 percent. A discount of 30 percent was given. What is the marked price of the article?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Use the ratio of **Marked Price (MP)** to **Cost Price (CP)**: MP / CP = (100 + **Profit%**) / (100 − **Discount%**) MP / 10000 = (100 + 40) / (100 − 30) = 140 / 70 = 2 / 1 MP = 10000 × 2 = ₹20000 **∴ The correct answer is ₹20000.**

questions.question: Which of the following will have the highest marked price?

options.text: Selling price = Rs. 4000 and Discount = 10 percent
Selling price = Rs. 5000 and Discount = 25 percent
Selling price = Rs. 6000 and Discount = 45 percent
Selling price = Rs. 6250 and Discount = 20 percent

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Marked Price (MP)** is calculated as **SP ÷ (1 − d)**, where d is the discount in decimal form.

Compare denominators: 0.9, 0.75, 0.55, and 0.8. A smaller denominator increases the final value.

Option 3: 6000 ÷ 0.55 ≈ 10909.09 (Highest SP with the highest discount %).

Option 4: 6250 ÷ 0.8 = 7812.5 (High SP but much lower discount %).

By inspection, Case 3 has the lowest multiplier (0.55) relative to its high base price.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 6000 and 45% discount.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Selling Price (SP)** and **Discount Percentage** for four different cases.

**Formula Used:** **Marked Price (MP)** = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount %)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b4d9dde2bd296aa2eda83d39b7ceb8df10fa5c4dd9df6e60db12596815ffd33.png] 

⇒ **Case 1:** MP = (4000 × 100) ÷ (100 − 10) = 400000 ÷ 90 ≈ **₹4444.44**

⇒ **Case 2:** MP = (5000 × 100) ÷ (100 − 25) = 500000 ÷ 75 ≈ **₹6666.67**

⇒ **Case 3:** MP = (6000 × 100) ÷ (100 − 45) = 600000 ÷ 55 ≈ **₹10909.09**

⇒ **Case 4:** MP = (6250 × 100) ÷ (100 − 20) = 625000 ÷ 80 = **₹7812.50**

Comparing all the results, Case 3 has the highest value.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 6000 and 45% discount.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

The **Marked Price (MP)** is also known as the list price or tag price. **Discount** is always calculated on the **MP**, and SP = MP − Discount.

Discount Percentage Formula

The percentage of discount is given by: **Discount %** = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts a% and b% are given, the **Effective Discount** = (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: After two successive discounts of 20 percent and 30 percent an article is sold for Rs. 4480. What is the marked price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net discount % = a + b − (a × b)/100

Net discount = 20 + 30 − (20 × 30)/100 = 50 − 6 = 44%

Selling Price (SP) = 100% − 44% = 56% of Marked Price

56% = Rs. 4480 ⇒ 1% = 80 ⇒ 100% = Rs. 8000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First discount (d₁) = 20%

Second discount (d₂) = 30%

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 4480

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7656fa993e84a49942d6a37879d079edc0bfbf4eb077c63130463e1063e1a4ac.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = MP × (80/100) × (70/100)

⇒ 4480 = MP × (4/5) × (7/10)

⇒ 4480 = MP × (28/50)

⇒ 4480 = MP × (14/25)

⇒ MP = (4480 × 25) ÷ 14

⇒ MP = 320 × 25

⇒ MP = Rs. 8000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 8000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the single equivalent discount is (x + y − xy/100)%.

Relationship between MP, CP and Profit/Discount

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Marked Price (MP) Definition

It is the price displayed on the label of an article, also known as the list price. Discount is always calculated on this price.

questions.question: A 1.8 meter tall boy casts a shadow 1.2 meter. At the same time a building casts a shadow 8 metre long. What is the height of the building?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Height** to **Shadow** is constant at the same time.

Boy's Ratio = 1.8 : 1.2 = 3 : 2

For the Building, Shadow = 8 m (which is 2 × 4)

Building Height = 3 × 4 = 12 m

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the **Boy** (H₁) = 1.8 m

Shadow of the **Boy** (S₁) = 1.2 m

Shadow of the **Building** (S₂) = 8 m

**Formula Used:**

In **Similar Triangles** (formed by sun rays), Height₁ / Shadow₁ = Height₂ / Shadow₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a424c6c5e57bd828f92336de35135e18fc7cb57805666185a17d6575eb72f98.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ H₁ / S₁ = H₂ / S₂

⇒ 1.8 / 1.2 = H₂ / 8

⇒ 3 / 2 = H₂ / 8

⇒ H₂ = (3 × 8) / 2

⇒ H₂ = 24 / 2

⇒ H₂ = 12 m

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

At any given time, the **Sun's angle of elevation** is the same for all objects in the same vicinity, making the triangles formed by objects and their shadows **mathematically similar**.

Properties of Similar Triangles

For two triangles to be similar, their **corresponding sides** must be in the same **proportion**. Here, Height/Shadow = tan(θ), where θ is the sun's altitude.

Ratio and Proportion

If a : b = c : d, then the product of means equals the product of extremes (ad = bc). This is used to find the unknown height directly.
